title: Time Variations in the Flux Density of Sgr A* at 230 GHz Detected with ALMA
question: Does Sgr A* show short-timescale (tens of minutes) variability at 230 GHz, and are there time lags between frequencies or a flux dependence of the spectral index?

what.value: Time lag of 30 min between 43 and 22 GHz used to predict expected lag

evidence.quote: Using the time lag $\Delta T_{\rm 2-1}$ between $\nu_2 = 43$ GHz and $\nu_1 = 22$ GHz of 30 min (cite: Yusef-Zadeh06; Yusef-Zadeh08)

recipe.method: standard calibration then iterative phase self-calibration
snapshot images per SPW and imfit flux measurement
key_parameters: integration 16-56 s; 44 or 45 snapshots per 70 min epoch

recipe.method: first-order structure function (15 log bins to 60 min) and Lomb-Scargle periodogram
ZDCF per epoch, quadratic fit to peaks
spectral index between 217.5 and 234.0 GHz at all data points vs 217.5 GHz flux

evidence.quote: The average flux densities of 217.5, 219.5, and 234.0 GHz were $2.912\pm0.331$, $2.914\pm0.331$, and $2.939\pm0.348$ Jy, respectively.
The mean spectral index of all the data is $0.12\pm0.10$.
The variation during epoch 6 at 234.0 GHz is delayed by $2.6\pm0.3$ min from that at 217.5 GHz.
precedes that at 217.5 GHz by $1.4\pm0.4$ min
The largest amplitude of flux variation (14%) can be seen during epoch 8

not_stated_but_needed: Imaging parameters (cell size, image size, imaging task, uv range)
Self-calibration solution intervals and number of iterations
Structure function and Lomb-Scargle details such as frequency grid
Number of SPW-combination choices for spectral index and the flux-scale correction between epochs
score_reason: Data identified and workflow simple, but key imaging and self-cal settings missing.
rediscovery_reason: Archive data with a simple recipe and numeric results (flux, lags, indices).
